name: Hen Wife

attributes.attribute: Scottish folkloric character whose Gaelic name is Cailleach nan Cearac
a woman keeping chickens on Highland farms was believed to have magical powers tied to witchcraft
a man running the same business was not given the same belief
may connect to the Cailleach as goddess of animals or to the perceived power of women earning a living by selling eggs and meat

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Hen Wife is a Scottish folkloric character. Her Gaelic name is Cailleach nan Cearac. On farms in the Scottish Highlands a woman who kept chickens was thought to have magical powers. People tied those powers to witchcraft. A man who ran the same business did not receive the same belief. The Hen Wife appears in several folktales. She may connect to the Cailleach as goddess of animals. She may also simply spring from the perceived power of women who earned their own living by selling eggs and meat.
objective: Document the Hen Wife, the Scottish chicken-keeping folkloric character.
key_results: Record her Gaelic name and her role on Highland farms.
Describe the belief in her magical powers and the witch link.
Note the contrast with men and the possible Cailleach connection.
